**Johnson & Johnson had the higher net margin in fiscal 2023, by about 37.7 percentage points.** I used figures I remember from the 10-Ks rather than searching, so treat them as approximate.

- **Pfizer:** Net income attributable to shareholders was about $2,119M on revenue of $58,496M, a net margin of about 3.6%.
- **Johnson & Johnson:** Net earnings were about $35,153M on sales of $85,159M, a net margin of about 41.3%. This figure includes a large one-time gain from the Kenvue separation (the exchange offer), so it overstates J&J's underlying profitability.

The gap is 41.3% − 3.6% ≈ 37.7 percentage points.
